cases.rationale: 8C's own documented genuine ranking miss (retrieval_miss_relevant=true, gold/candidates/jango1324.json). This repo's GitHub-reported primary_language is Python; ml_engineering_01 requires language.python (REQUIRED) -- recoverable via the cheap structured language-field signal alone, no description/topics needed. Genuinely relevant AND successfully recovered by job-aware retrieval.

general_swe_01's sole technical requirement is an alternative group ['language.cpp','language.java','language.python'] (Proficiency in at least one of Python, Java, or C++) -- demonstrates ANY-side alternative-group relevance end-to-end (Part 4), not just in isolated unit tests. Genuinely relevant AND recovered via the same language.python match as the ml_engineering_01 case.

GENUINELY RELEVANT -- this is a real ML-education repository and this repo's primary_language is 'Jupyter Notebook', which DOES earn real, correct relevance (score 0.5, the PREFERRED weight for computer_vision_01's language.jupyter_notebook term -- confirmed via score_repository_relevance() directly). It is still NOT ANALYZED (expected_analyzed=false) because karpathy's account has 39 total repositories scoring >0 for this job (mostly 1.0-2.0, matching the REQUIRED language.python/ml.framework.pytorch/platform.cuda terms), and this repo ranks 38th of 39 by score -- far outside the default relevance_top_k=10. This MUST be reported as a missed relevant repository (classify_retrieval_outcome -> RETRIEVAL_MISSED_RELEVANT), never as a correctly-excluded negative control -- the relevance signal correctly identifies it as relevant; the fixed top-10 budget still excludes it because so many OTHER repos score higher. Increasing relevance_top_k specifically to recover this one case would be tuning the budget to this evaluation rather than choosing it on its own merits (Milestone brief: 'conservative defaults based on the existing top_n=15 behavior') -- documented as a known limitation instead (docs/evaluation/MILESTONE_8D2_JOB_AWARE_RETRIEVAL.md).

GENUINE NEGATIVE CONTROL for the same repository as the case above: frontend_01's required concepts are language.javascript/language.typescript/framework.react/language.css -- none of which this Jupyter-Notebook ML repo's language field or free text plausibly satisfies. Demonstrates recovery is JOB-SPECIFIC, never a blanket 'always retrieve this repo' rule (Milestone brief's explicit warning), and that the SAME repository can be genuinely relevant to one job (the case above) and genuinely irrelevant to another.

GENUINELY RELEVANT -- a well-engineered, widely-used JavaScript process-execution library, and this repo's primary_language is JavaScript, which DOES earn real, correct relevance (score 1.0, matching fullstack_01's REQUIRED language.javascript term -- confirmed via score_repository_relevance() directly). It is still NOT ANALYZED (expected_analyzed=false) because sindresorhus has 1,142 repositories and 992 of them score >0 for this job (the account is overwhelmingly JavaScript/TypeScript, so a single language-field match is a very weak discriminator here) -- execa ties at score 1.0 with hundreds of others and ranks 231st of 992 by the deterministic name-ascending tie-break, far outside relevance_top_k=10. This MUST be reported as a missed relevant repository (RETRIEVAL_MISSED_RELEVANT), never as a correctly-excluded negative control. This is the SAME underlying problem 8C's own evaluation named for this exact account/repository (an extremely prolific account defeats any small fixed cutoff) -- Stage-2 retrieval narrows but does not eliminate it for a single-weak-signal match on a 1000+-repository account; a stronger/more specific job requirement (matching execa's own topics -- 'exec', 'spawn', 'child-process' -- none of which any job in this corpus names) or a larger budget would be needed, and is documented as a known limitation rather than forced via a larger default (docs/evaluation/MILESTONE_8D2_JOB_AWARE_RETRIEVAL.md).

GENUINE NEGATIVE CONTROL for the same repository: robotics_controls_01 requires robotics.ros2/language.python/language.cpp -- none of which a JavaScript process-execution library's language field or free text (topics: binary, child-process, exec, nodejs, shell, spawn...) plausibly satisfies.

GENUINE NEGATIVE CONTROL against a hugely-starred but genuinely low-substance repository (a curated markdown link-list, no real 'language', gold/candidates/sindresorhus.json's own documented DELIBERATE deprioritization -- not a retrieval miss). Must not be pulled in by job relevance either: its description/topics (awesome, awesome-list, lists, resources, unicorns) share no concept with frontend_01's JS/TS/React/CSS requirements. Confirms job-aware retrieval does not simply chase star count or any common word.
